content.title: About
content.content: Chicken tenders or strips are pieces of chicken breast coated in seasoned breadcrumbs and fried or baked until golden. They are a common component of school lunches, providing a quick source of protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken tenders became popular in the United States in the 1970s and spread to school cafeterias worldwide.
In many school menus the strips are made from whole breast fillets without bones.
The breading often includes spices such as paprika, garlic, and onion for extra flavor.
Most manufacturers use vegetable oils for frying, keeping the product affordable.
Some schools serve the strips with dipping sauces like barbecue or honey‑mustard.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken provides complete protein essential for growth, muscle repair, and satiety.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Nutrients such as niacin, B6, and B12 support energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: When eaten in moderation, breaded strips fit well into low‑carb eating plans.

items.title: Provides iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals are important for immune function and blood formation.

items.title: Promotes fullness
items.content: The combination of protein and a modest amount of fat helps keep you satisfied longer.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The breadcrumb coating often contains salt; people monitoring sodium intake should limit portions.

items.title: Trans and saturated fats
items.content: Frying can create trans fats; baked versions are a healthier alternative.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Although rare, some individuals may be allergic to chicken proteins.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Some brands add preservatives and flavor enhancers that may be undesirable for sensitive consumers.

items.title: Choking hazard for young children
items.content: Small breadcrumb pieces can pose a choking risk for toddlers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the tenders hot as a snack, add them to salads, wraps, or grain bowls, and pair with sauces such as ketchup, mustard, yogurt dip, or soy sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked tenders in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Frozen portions last up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.
